# Riprap

> Purpose pools on Solana, settled by peers. Any group can start a pool for one purpose, fixed at creation — mutual cover for what goes wrong, bounties for verified acts, a purpose of the group's own beside them; risk capital and yield on the roadmap. Peer jurors adjudicate every payout against the pool's purpose, unused funds return to members pro-rata, finite pools dissolve. Pre-launch.

Riprap is a protocol for purpose pools on Solana: any group can start one — chip in under a purpose you set, drawn peers decide every payout against it, the money stays the group's. The purpose never changes; a new purpose is a new pool. The first markets are pooled cover (the risks insurers can't sell) and verified-act bounties. In a cover pool, members pay a fixed entry fee against one narrowly defined peril; a qualifying incident is adjudicated by jurors drawn from the pool's own staked members (adjudication runs on Accord, a Schelling-point arbitration protocol; voting coherently with the honest majority is the profitable strategy). Approved requests pay out of the pool; payouts are capped twice, by the member's tier and by the pool's balance. When the request window closes, every unused cent returns to members pro-rata and the pool dissolves permanently. A bounty pool is the same rails pointed the other way: it pays for verified acts instead of losses. No insurer, no reserve, no retained profit. Roadmap: outside risk capital stakes into pools and earns a rule-set share of the surplus — insurance, rebuilt as rails.

Money leaves a pool through exactly two governed doors: spending (adjudicated requests) and liquidation. There is no third exit and no discretionary signer.

## Pages

- [Platform landing](https://riprap.xyz/): purpose pools settled by peers, the pools directory, the five-step lifecycle, twelve honest FAQ answers, waitlist. The peril never appears in the platform copy; the directory cards carry each pool's own peril, per its policy.
- [The pools](https://riprap.xyz/#/pools): the tabular pool directory — every live pool, mutual and bounty alike, with what it covers or pays for, its entry fees, and its maximum payouts. The legacy `#/mutuals` hash still resolves to the same page. Hash route: renders client-side from the landing document.
- [Pool details](https://riprap.xyz/#/m/blade-pool): every pool resolves at #/m/<pool-pubkey-or-slug> — the Blade Pool's full policy page (legacy #/2026-breakpoint-blade-pool route kept), and a placeholder detail page per draft pool (definition, exclusions, request proof, worked math, the end) extracted from its policy/terms document. Hash routes: render client-side from the landing document.
- [App](https://riprap.xyz/#/app): the member wallet surface — a table of every pool the connected wallet joined on this cluster, each row with its own filing and jury-duty actions. Hash route: renders client-side from the landing document.
- [File a payout request](https://riprap.xyz/#/app/file-claim/DtjVEhcrESkED2Mc57smYE5doGxRSi4TK3bP2zqGEccF): the payout-request wizard, scoped to one pool by its route id — the incident, the five required proofs, one on-chain request. Each entered pool's app row links its own wizard at `#/app/file-claim/<pool>`. Hash route: renders client-side from the landing document.
- [Restore a filed request](https://riprap.xyz/#/app/file-claim/DtjVEhcrESkED2Mc57smYE5doGxRSi4TK3bP2zqGEccF/restore/0): the read-only replay of a pending request — the manifest reads back from the evidence operator (or re-uploads from the kept manifest.yaml), verifies against the on-chain hash, and evidence can be re-delivered. Reached from a PENDING request row on the app surface. Hash route: renders client-side from the landing document.
- [Create a pool](https://riprap.xyz/#/create): the pool-authoring wizard — write a pool's own terms (the qualifying peril or the paid act, entry tiers, the event window, the required proof), preview the exact terms document with its on-chain anchors, then deploy and publish the pool from the browser. Hash route: renders client-side from the landing document.

## Pools in the first batch (Breakpoint 2026)

- Blade Pool — knife assault cover: bodily injury caused by another person with a knife or blade during the conference. Tiers: $10/$20/$40 entry, up to $1,000/$2,000/$4,000 payout (final). Live surface: the pool page above.
- NGMI Hairline — new gray hair first visible during the conference, graded I–IV ("a countable few" to "basically Gandalf"). Fixed $25 entry, up to $200 payout; grades pay $20/$60/$100/$200 — 10/30/50/100% of the maximum (final, policy §5).
- OnlyFriends (bounty) — confirmed introductions of a member to a listed VIP, paid per introduction. Draft: $25 entry, $15 per intro up to $150 (TODO-confirm in terms).
- Operation Keep Raj Warm / Lily's Liquid Lifeline / Toly Needs His Fuel (bounties) — bring the named person (Raj Gokal, Lily Liu, Anatoly Yakovenko) a hot drink they asked for, hand to hand, still hot, confirmed by them. Draft: $5 entry, $50 bounty each (TODO-confirm in terms). Bounties share no risk — they pay for verified acts on the same rails as the mutuals.
- Caffeine Supercycle (bounty) — the merged hot-drink pool: bring Lily Liu, Anatoly "Toly" Yakovenko, or Raj Gokal a hot drink they asked for, hand to hand, still hot, confirmed by them; one pot pays at most ten deliveries across the roster, in the order their requests are approved. $5 entry, up to $50 bounty (final, terms §5). The three single-person hot-drink pools stay deployed on devnet.
- Mert of the Year (bounty) — hand Mert Mumtaz an over-the-top trophy bearing the required inscription ("For Outstanding Contributions to Making Solana Developers Less Miserable."), delivered with a completely serious thirty-second acceptance speech on his behalf, notified on X tagging @riprapxyz; the bounty pays the one trophy he declares best after the conference. $10 entry, $1000 bounty (final, terms §5; his consent and the adjudication fee are TODO in the terms).

## Policy: Blade Pool @ Breakpoint 2026 (the first pool)

- Peril: knife assault — bodily injury caused by another person intentionally using a knife or bladed instrument against the member.
- Event window: 15–17 November 2026 — opens with the conference, closes with the conference (daily hours per the published event schedule).
- Event area: Olympia Convention Centre and designated event area, London.
- Tiers: Basic $10 entry, max payout $1,000 · Standard $20 entry, max payout $2,000 · Premium $40 entry, max payout $4,000. The max payout is the total a member can receive for qualifying requests from the qualifying event.
- Exclusions (not paid): injuries caused by the member themselves; accidental injuries involving a knife or blade; ordinary handling or use of a knife; consensual activities; incidents outside the event window; incidents outside the event area; emotional distress without qualifying bodily injury; requests exceeding the member's tier maximum.
- Requests: a member files a request with evidence for a qualifying incident during the window; jurors drawn from this pool's staked members adjudicate it. If approved requests exceed the funds in the pool, payouts are reduced proportionally — the pool never pays more than it holds.
- End: after the conference, the request window, and settlement of approved requests, the remaining pool balance is distributed to members and the pool dissolves permanently. No funds remain.

- Status: pre-launch. No pool has run, no members exist, no payouts to show. The first pool is the build target, not a track record.
